entities.summary: Quintus Aemilius Laetus was a Roman military officer and Praetorian Guard prefect under the emperors Commodus and Pertinax. His role in the assassination of Commodus and the subsequent Year of the Five Emperors had far-reaching consequences for the Roman Empire. Laetus played a key part in the transition from the Julio-Claudian dynasty to the Year of the Five Emperors, a period of political instability and power struggles that would ultimately shape the course of Roman history. His actions had a lasting impact on the Praetorian Guard's role in Roman politics and the nature of imperial succession.
